value.rationale: The general theorem p>=17 had precisely two smaller prime cases p11 and p13 not settled by its inequality; proving both impossible establishes sharp prime threshold p>=11, with a geometrically smooth p7 boundary. The cases are forced by the natural Hasse–Blokhuis equality, and all cubic plane embeddings—not an arbitrary sample—are classified.
